title: Null pointers, null pointer constants and safe checks
learningObjectives: Explain the language rule and its constraints.
Trace the example and predict its behaviour.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: A null pointer value is guaranteed to compare unequal to a pointer to any object or function. The macro NULL expands to an implementation-defined null pointer constant. A pointer can be checked against NULL before dereferencing when null is an allowed state.
understand.whyItMatters: This knowledge helps reason about C data representation, object bounds and valid memory access.
understand.analogy: Think of memory objects as labelled storage and pointers as typed references to that storage.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal pointer, lifetime and object-access rules.

explain.narrative:
A null pointer value is guaranteed to compare unequal to a pointer to any object or function. The macro NULL expands to an implementation-defined null pointer constant. A pointer can be checked against NULL before dereferencing when null is an allowed state.

Check the declared types, object lifetime, valid bounds and function preconditions before using the construct. Enable compiler warnings and test edge cases.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.code: Null represents the absence of a valid target. Checking it prevents one common invalid dereference, but it does not prove that a non-null pointer is valid or that its object is still alive.

practise.guidedTask: The pointer is initialized to the address of value, then checked before dereferencing. If ptr were NULL, the body would be skipped.
practise.independentTask: Explain why a NULL check does not detect every dangling pointer.
hints: Write a function that accepts an optional int pointer and safely handles the NULL case.
Use NULL for pointer values; use 0 or '\0' only according to the context and intended type.
A non-null pointer can still be invalid or dangling.
